sec-bot: [ALERT] KMS key policy change detected for projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/infra/cryptoKeys/infra-1
sec-bot: change by principal: terraform-ci@redwood-svc.iam.gserviceaccount.com at 2026-05-03T14:20:12Z
sec-bot: policy diff:
```
- members: [
-   serviceAccount:sa-backup@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com
+ members: [
+   allAuthenticatedUsers
]
```

Maria: seeing the same in audit-logs; looks like a badly templated iam_binding in the infra pipeline. :eyes:
Maria: attaching minimal audit line: `methodName=SetIamPolicy resource=cryptoKeys/infra-1 actor=terraform-ci@redwood-svc.iam.gserviceaccount.com`

Ken: simultaneous alert from network-monitoring: ephemeral firewall rule opened to 0.0.0.0/0 for ports 1024-65535 on subnet inference-prod created ~14:20:45Z by `automation/instance-provisioner`
Ken: suspect CI job that applies terraform + a parallel automation that updates instance metadata.

Alex: containment plan: 1) remove `allAuthenticatedUsers` binding from KMS key policy 2) disable the terraform-ci SA keys and revoke active OAuth tokens 3) create a new key version and disable old key until audit complete 4) block the ephemeral firewall rule and add host-level iptables deny if needed

Sloan: agree. Also enable org-policy and add a policy to block `allUsers`/`allAuthenticatedUsers` in KMS key bindings via policy-library guard. This looks like a template variable collapse.

oncall: executing containment steps now:
```
# remove public member from key
gcloud kms keys remove-iam-policy-binding infra-1 \ 
  --location global \ 
  --keyring infra \ 
  --member="allAuthenticatedUsers" \ 
  --role="roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter"

# disable terraform CI SA keys
gcloud iam service-accounts keys disable --iam-account=terraform-ci@redwood-svc.iam.gserviceaccount.com --key-file=auto-detected || true

# block firewall rule
gcloud compute firewall-rules update ephemeral-ci-allow --disabled
```

oncall: done removing public binding and disabling firewall rule, logs show call IDs: 0a3f... , 0b7e...

Maria: good, start key rotation next: create key version, re-encrypt any active material if needed, and mark previous versions disabled pending review. Notify product owners for any downtime risk.

Alex: also rotate any credentials that may have been readable by that key (service tokens for backup jobs). Run a quick scan for resources encrypted with infra-1: `gcloud asset search-all-resources --query="kmsKey:infra-1"`

Ken: I'll sweep all instances provisioned in last 48h for suspicious docker images and startup scripts. If we see unexpected artifacts, we'll isolate host and snapshot disk.

sec-bot: Audit log export confirms logs for SetIamPolicy and Compute firewall change were delivered to sec-logs-bucket and BigQuery dataset `sec_audit.events` for correlation.

Sloan: Post-incident actions (owner: Sloan):
- run terraform drift detection across infra repo and pin modules
- add a pre-apply validation hook that rejects `allUsers`/`allAuthenticatedUsers` in KMS bindings
- add a guardrail to pipeline templating to fail on empty variables that affect member lists
- 30-day audit of SA key usage and token lifetime settings

Alex: I've opened an incident PRD and assigned follow-ups: rotate keys (Alex), SA lockdown (Maria), firewall audit (Ken), templating fix + pre-apply hook (Sloan). Please update checklist in the incident doc.

Maria: legal and customer-ops looped in — they want a short timeline and confirmation no data exfiltration.

Ken: initial forensics shows no external downloads from affected VMs in the 2h window. will update if that changes.

Sloan: thanks team. quick wins: enforce policy-library check and add terraform deny rule in CI. Longer: kms policy linting and improved audit-alert thresholds. :thumbsup:

Alex: marking containment complete for now. will keep this thread updated with postmortem link once drafted.
